reviews.title: Good premise, but…
reviews.text:
While this app works well in visual design, variability, and aesthetics, it doesn’t do too well with the actual facts it uses (specifically, the sources it draws from).

As someone who is an avid reader of all things interesting, I love to read more on cool topics— to which this app may introduce you to many (fantastic). However, I question the validity of the sources used to obtain a lot of the facts, especially from websites that will pull from third-party sources who usually end up oversimplifying or skewing results to generate better engagement.

The other thing regarding the sources used, is that while it’s intuitive to find the direct source, there is no direct way for individuals to report a fact for misleading content/ misinformation (a lot of which is arguably more harmful than helpful, especially in regards to psychological and scientific-related facts).

It would be best to have a more thorough/ vetted process of facts, as well as a way to “expand” the notification to show not only more detail on individual facts, but also show the direct source link through the banner notifications without having to unlock your phone to access the information (ie; citing the source in APA/ MLA).

reviews.title: The facts are WRONG.
reviews.text:
Some of the facts that pop up feel like those “7 foods that your doctor doesn’t want you to know about!” Where it claims horribly misconstrued myths and science pulled out of context.

One I just saw was “Eating bananas can help fight depression” 
I tapped on the “source” and the page said NOTHING of the sort. It only spoke about the importance of meditation, laughter, a sense of purpose, etc. Not even a single mention of “banana”.

So I actually looked into it: Bananas contain tryptophan and vitamin B-6 used for making serotonin, and also contains small amounts of serotonin itself, BUT none of it crosses the blood-brain barrier, and research has shown limited/inconclusive evidence. 

And this is just ONE of many “facts” I looked further into. 

So… why do I even own this app if it’s telling me “facts” that have no source, and no confirmed evidence that it’s true? 

It breaks my heart that so many people are giving this app a high review. Some of these “facts” are incorrect HEALTH facts. You’re actively hurting people into believing misinformation.

reviews.title: Good overall
reviews.text:
Love the app, widgets, and notifications. And I’m someone that hardly ever turns notifications on. Been using the app about a month or two now and would scroll endlessly, soaking up all of the intriguing info. I’m constantly annoying my teenagers with the fun facts I find most interesting. They’ve even asked to download it themselves now.

I appreciate that you can favorite as many as you want. I also love that there are links to articles! Sometimes they’re outdated or don’t work, but that’s understandable when there are so many facts and you can’t control it if the source removes or moves it. They work majority of the time, so it’s not a big deal. If it’s something super interesting I want to read more about in those cases I just google it.

The ONLY complaint I have that knocked off a star (but it’s a big one) is that after using the app for a few weeks, it’s now switched to half or more facts being trivia/question-answer format. I noticed the app name and icon have changed towards that as well. I find it awkward and really annoying to read it that way. I also feel like the trivia-like “facts” are way less interesting bc the idea is that someone might know the answer. Whereas the facts before were really obscure and I had never heard them before, so I was learning interesting things, not testing knowledge I might already have. There are plenty of trivia apps out there - let this one just be straight facts. Or, show the fact as the main thing and on the notification/widget, but when opened, below the fact you can show it formatted as trivia. That way if someone wants to scroll through and use it as trivia questions they can.
